sections.title: Hotel Operations (Pan Pacific Hotels Group)
sections.subtitle: ~25% of group revenue; occupancy and RevPAR by region

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For UOL Group Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For UOL Group Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For UOL Group Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For UOL Group Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

hotelOccupancy.title: Hotel occupancy by region
hotelOccupancy.content:
Occupancy is the share of available hotel rooms sold, reported by Pan Pacific Hotels Group for its Singapore, Oceania (Australia/New Zealand) and Others (China, Malaysia, Myanmar, Vietnam, US) portfolios.

For UOL Group Limited: hospitality is roughly a quarter of group revenue and the most cyclical segment -- occupancy is the volume half of RevPAR's volume-times-rate split, and both recovered steadily post-pandemic through FY2025.

What to watch:

  • Singapore occupancy against the broader market (tourism arrivals, MICE calendar)
  • Oceania/Others occupancy lagging or leading Singapore (portfolio maturity, new openings)
  • Occupancy plateauing while RevPAR keeps rising signals rate-led rather than volume-led growth

hotelRevpar.title: Hotel RevPAR by region
hotelRevpar.content:
RevPAR (revenue per available room) is average daily rate multiplied by occupancy -- the standard hotel-industry yield metric, shown here in S$ per region.

For UOL Group Limited: Singapore RevPAR is structurally the highest of the three regions and the main driver of hospitality segment revenue; Oceania and Others are smaller but have grown faster off a lower base through FY2025 and the H1 FY2026 interim.

What to watch:

  • Singapore RevPAR against room-supply growth on the island
  • Whether Oceania/Others RevPAR gains hold once occupancy plateaus (rate power vs. one-off volume recovery)
  • RevPAR growth versus group revenue growth -- confirms how much of the swing is the hotel segment

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For UOL Group Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For UOL Group Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For UOL Group Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For UOL Group Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For UOL Group Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For UOL Group Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
